title: Tucson gay bar shooting: Two killed outside bar in ‘targeted attack’ on the LGBTQ community, police say | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A deadly shooting in the parking lot of a gay bar near downtown Tucson, Arizona, early Monday morning was “a targeted attack motivated by hate toward the LGBTQIA+ community,” police said.

Two people, Vincent Anthony Siqueiros, 42, and Cameron Davis Capara, 33, were killed in the shooting outside of Venture-N, a longtime Tucson gay bar the Tucson Police Department said in astatement.

The gunman was identified as 44-year-old Ousman Ceesay, who died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said. He had a note on him listing several LGBTQ-associated businesses, according to an earlierpolice statement.

Ceesay had recently arrived in the Tucson area and had no apparent connection to the victims, investigators said. During a search of his residence, police found evidence the attack was targeted at the LGBTQ community and a note indicating he acted alone, the police statement said.

“It’s just heartbreaking. Such a senseless, tragic shooting,” LGBTQ community member Scott Blades toldCNN-affiliate KOLD. “This is a real important community gathering spot, and it’s always been a safe place for people to come.”

Colette Barajas, the owner and broker of Centra Realty, has been a longstanding member of the LGBTQ community and displays a rainbow flag outside her business and home.

“I’m nervous, you know, I’ve got my flag out there,” Barajas said in an interview with KOLD.

Community members placed candles and flowers outside the bar in memory of the shooting victims.

“We’ll keep finding ways to create that community and find ways to create safety for ourselves and for each other. That’s all we can do,” Blades added.

In response to the shooting, the Tucson Police Department increased its presence around gay establishments, Police Chief Monica Prieto said in a statement.

“I am deeply saddened that another senseless loss of life has happened in our community. Bias-based crimes are especially heinous and have no place in our community,” Prieto said.

Prieto said there was no indication of an ongoing threat to the public.

Jose Ortega, the property owner of Venture-N, told CNN that he was out of town on a trip to Mexico when he learned about the incident.

The acting manager called around 1 a.m. on Monday saying something happened outside in the parking lot and one of the victims came in the door bleeding, saying he was shot, Ortega said.

“It was terrible, we didn’t know what to say,” Ortega added. He returned from his trip with his business partner David Wallis, the owner of Venture-N, early after learning what had happened.

Ortega describes Venture-N as “one of the only gar bars left” with a lot of regular patrons.

“It’s a gay bar, but a neighborhood bar,” Ortega said. He added the shooting victims were people who came to the bar fairly regularly. No one from the bar has ever seen or heard of the shooter, according to Ortega.

“This really has to be kind of an outlier. It has to be just something strange that happened,” Ortega said. “Unfortunately, we’re the ones that were affected this time.”

Ortega explained that everyone gets along in Tucson.

“There’s no way to express sorrow and sympathy in a proper way,” Ortega added.

Organizations and community leaders expressed an outpouring of support following the shooting. The Southern Arizona AIDS Foundation plans to hold an event on Wednesday to honor the victims.

“This tragedy serves as yet another painful reminder that homophobia is still rampant in our country,” Tucson Mayor Regina Romero said in a video message on her Facebook page.

“No one should fear being targeted simply because of who they are and where they gather. I speak in solidarity with our LGBTQ+ community,” Pima County Attorney Laura Conover said in a statement.

The police department said the investigation is ongoing.
